project.analysisThroughputDescription: Actual effort (person-hours) of completed activities, stacked by assignee and bucketed by the week of their actual completion date. Measuring by effort rather than count absorbs differences in task size, showing who did how much work and when. The effort efficiency at the top is planned effort ÷ actual effort (efficiency vs estimate, i.e. EVM CPI). When there are many assignees, the top contributors are shown individually and the rest are grouped as 'Others'. Activities with no actual effort entered do not appear in the bars and are excluded from the efficiency calculation.
project.analysisVarianceDescription: For completed activities, compares the planned effort (entered by PM/PL) and the actual effort (entered by the assignee) side by side per assignee. Only tasks where both are available (completed and actual effort entered) are counted, making it a useful reference for reviewing estimation accuracy and task allocation. Hovering a bar shows planned, actual, and their difference (actual − planned; + over, − under). When there are many assignees, the top 8 by actual effort are shown individually and the rest grouped as 'Others'.
project.analysisWorkloadDescription: Planned effort of incomplete tasks (not started / in progress), stacked by status per assignee. On-hold tasks are excluded. Compare who has the most remaining work and who is lighter, as input for balancing load and allocating tasks. The toggle offers two views: 'Assigned amount' is the planned effort as-is, while 'Pace-adjusted' multiplies each assignee's planned effort by their historical actual/planned ratio to estimate remaining hours (no adjustment for those without history). Planned effort is an estimate and the same task takes different people different time, so use this as input for allocation decisions only — not as a precise burden measure or for evaluating individuals. When there are many assignees, the top 8 by workload are shown individually and the rest grouped as 'Others'.
project.analysisCapacityDescription: Distributes the planned effort of incomplete tasks (not started / in progress) evenly across each day and lays out the per-day effort for each assignee by date (today onward) as a heatmap. The daily cap is 8 hours: cells over 7h are amber (warning) and over 8h are red (over). Use it to spot days where work piles up (overload) early, and to consider leveling the load by shifting schedules or reassigning work. The most stretched assignees appear at the top. Note that the distribution is an even-split approximation over the planned period and does not reflect actual work allocation or weekends/holidays. Because the same effort takes different people different amounts of time, treat this as a hint for noticing uneven load, not as an exact workload measure or individual evaluation. Completed and on-hold tasks are excluded.

migrationImport.descriptionBefore: This feature bulk-imports knowledge and other data accumulated in other services into this tenant. The available operation is therefore
migrationImport.descriptionAfter: , and bulk updating of existing data is not supported. To bulk update, use the individual list screens in each project.
migrationImport.step1: Click the relevant button in the 'Download template CSV (optional)' section below to download the CSV template.
migrationImport.step2: Open the downloaded CSV and fill in the relevant columns.
migrationImport.step3: Click 'Next: Mapping' and map Tasukiba field names to your CSV columns on the mapping screen.
migrationImport.step4: Click 'Next: Confirm preview' to check the import count and any errors.
migrationImport.step5: Verify that the import count matches and no errors are shown, then click 'Import this data'.
